newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end sharply lower, but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end sharply lower, but off lows.

text.p: Swiss shares ended markedly lower, but off the day's lows in quiet trade as sagging futures on blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) put pressure on the stocks.

Weaker-than-expected U.S. consumer confidence data lent shares some support in the second half of the session, but investors were likely to remain sidelined ahead of U.S. presidential elections, a dealer said.
"We may see a further decline in prices", he added.
The blue-chip SMI ended 31.5 points lower, or 0.84 percent, at 3,732.0 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 19.46 points, or 0.81 percent, to 2,395.80 points.
Most blue chips were lower, but Alusuisse stood out because it added three francs to 937.
Most-active Roche gave up 95 francs or 0.99 percent to 9,520. Other pharmaceuticals also gave up ground, partially due to losses in U.S. pharma stocks, a dealer said.
CS Holding and UBS were among the biggest losers among financials, slumping more than one percent each. Insurer Baloise gave up some of its recent strong advances, sliding 1.31 percent.

Shares of freight forwarding group Danzas soared three percent. Dealers attributed the rise to road shows for investors the group was said to be preparing ond to forthcoming research studies which were said to be positive.
Shares and certificates of brewery group Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann, which said it will close three of its five breweries in Switzerland, lost ground.
Shares of beverage group Sibra, which is majority owned by Feldschloesschen, jumped more than 30 percent. Feldschloesschen said it planned to merge with Sibra.
